data.name: Monsters and Monocles
data.detailed_description:
Monsters and Monocles is a frantic, Victorian steampunk themed twin-stick shooter all about using teamwork and heavy weaponry to battle the hordes of evil. A naive occult collector has unknowingly unleashed a great evil that is spreading across the globe, and it’s up to you and a team of quirky paranormal investigators to find the source of this dark energy and blast it back to where it came from.

Online and Local Multiplayer


Take on the challenge solo, or play with up to 4 players online or locally. Your team shares a single pool of lives so you need to stick together, revive fallen comrades, and watch each other’s backs.

Customize Your Play Style


Search out and use powerful weapons to aid you in battle like the blunderbuss, stake launcher and the crumpet cannon - a steampunk toaster that fires weaponized crumpets.
Find and equip relics to customize your weapons and add new abilities to match your play style, and upgrade them by looting chests and destroying enemies.

Procedurally Generated World


Each level is procedural so you and your comrades will be faced with unique enemy placement, traps, secrets and objectives each time you play. Your trusty airship the HMS Scone acts as your hub and lets you gear up before taking on challenging levels like the haunted mansion, snowy Victorian streets and a cursed Pharaoh’s tomb. Each area ends with a fearsome boss encounter, such as a demonic chimney sweep or a giant cyclops skull.


Features


  • 4 player co-op - both locally and online
  • Co-op centric gameplay - Revive teammates and shared pool of lives across all players
  • Challenging single player
  • Every game is different - Procedural levels, enemies, relics, objectives, and secrets
  • Customizable abilities - Collect relics that can be upgraded across play sessions to match your play style
  • Full Controller support
  • Huge bosses
  • Sound design & Music by Hyperduck Soundworks
  • Dogs wearing smoking jackets

data.short_description: Monsters and Monocles is a frantic top-down shooter for 1-4 players. Use teamwork and your arsenal of weapons to defeat the overwhelming hordes of evil, either locally or online. All the levels are procedurally generated with new layouts, objectives, and secrets each time you play.

reviews.review:
[h1]200 character summary[/h1]
Monsters and Monocles is a great rogue lite twin stick shooter with a lot of weapons, items, different biomes and random generated floors. You can play the game with up to 4 players locally or online.

[h1]Story & Characters [b]7/10[/b][/h1]
The game starts with a small intro without dialogue, so this is my intepretation of it, There is some Wizard? and when he opens a pot ghosts fly out and strange phenomenom happen. Then the 4 playable characters read about it in the news and decide they are the ones to fix it. I think the drawings are very nice, but how does that wizards mansion explain the forest, tomb or city, And how does it explain the Dog with a Gun? You do collect fragments every time you kill a book, 4 fragments create a page which tells a bit about the story, But they are cryptic at best. I hope they will put in a bit more lore, a bit more mystery to uncover.

The characters are nice and unique, but they lack a backstory and some personality, Like a few one liners could tell a lot about a person, I also think 4 are not nearly enough for a 4 player game, There is a great diversity in shopkeepers and enemies, It is just a shame most appear in all levels.

[h1]Gamemodes & Gameplay [b]8/10[/b][/h1]
The game has 1 gamemode, Online and local are the same. You start out in the Airship and if you die anywhere all your progress will reset and you will start at the airship again. Here you can change your starting relics and upgrade them, You can trade in fragments for journal pages, and you can start a run by standing on a biome tile. You will spawn in level 1 of your chosen biome, The map is completely random but there is an arrow pointing to the exit. The maps are full with chests, enemies, NPCs and secrets.

Enemies drop money and sometimes health pickups. Chests can contain coins, weapons items and even relics. Secret areas are mostly accessable by a ladder under a destructable prop or trough hidden paths, You mostly find big chests here and sometimes big tea pots which drop a lot of health pickups. Once you find the exit you enter level 2, If you find the exit again you reach level 3 and this is the boss. If you beat the boss soul gems will drop, These are like the currency you don't lose when dying

The game currently has over 30 weapons, some are better than others, but it all depends on your preference and playstyle. There are over 20 items you can pick up in your runs, Most items have a good and a bad perk, Like Speed up, Defence down. but some are all good. Then there are over 20 Relics, They are rare but once you find them you keep them even if you die. You can carry 3 relics at a time and change which ones in the airship.

When you beat a boss you return to the airship, You can then start a second run, Each biome you complete the game gets a bit harder, and if you completed all biomes without dying you can loop and do it again while the game keeps getting harder.

[h1]Graphics & Soundtrack [b]8/10[/b][/h1]
The game has a pixel style old english theme to it, You drink tea for health, The clothing is just straight from victorian times. I really like the graphics tho, And I especially love the 2 English themed levels, The Mansion and The City.

The biomes look great, there is a lot of variation in props, some things are more generic props, but they are working on that to make the biomes feel more unique, The bosses fit the biomes, but the enemies could fit better. The enemies do look great, The game really has some great pixel art.

The soundtrack might get a bit repetitive over time, It has a nice soundtrack but it just has 1 track for each biome, one for the shops and one for the airship, more music would certainly help the game.

[h1]Performance & Support [b]8/10[/b][/h1]
The game runs very well, Everything just works, It is locked to your framerate which is a bit of a bummer, Adding some extra fps settings allows people to play it on extremely slow hardware and it would also make it more future proof for when 480Hz will be the default. Still I had no crashes, no bugs, no nothing, It just works great.

[h1]Endgame & Replayability [b]9/10[/b][/h1]
The game scores well in replayability, The Relics which enable you to customize your starting character, The multiplayer modes, The different biomes and procedural generation makes this game one to be played over and over again.

[h1]Improvements[/h1]
The multiplayer camera definitely needs to get fixed, It is not consistent, Sometimes people walk off and the screen follows them leaving the others off screen, and other times they just walk off the screen while keeping focus on a certain area. Preferrably the camera would zoom out till a certain level or the game would switch between shared and split screen like seen in Streets of Rogue. 4 playable characters is also the bare minimum, We should have more playable characters, Maybe unlockables?

Random generation is a great thing, But it feels a bit too random, I sometimes get entire levels without any weapon chest, Or sometimes I get completely overrun in the first room I enter in level 1-1. I also notice I get a lot of the same items in some runs, Like I don't need a third copy of that item I can't pick up anyway. Or maybe let us scrap items/weapons we don't want to use for cash like we see in Dead Cells. Custom seeds would also be nice to create a more consistent experience.

I want to see what an item does before I pick it up, or give me the ability to drop items, I understand the witch with the 3 pots should remain a non droppable mystery because you drink it, but I think pickups should be droppable, And a small dialogue box with the effects would really help a lot of players. More Items would also be great.

More Enemy variation between biomes, I see a lot of enemies being reused in all biomes, unique monsters would make the biomes feel a lot more special, Surely we also need more biomes itself, I especially love the mansion and the city, But the other 2 are great too, They are more open than the ones I like, I think it is nice there is also a difference in how rooms generate between the biomes and I would love to see that more.

[h1]Early Access[/h1]
The game is in Early Access, And it has been for a long time, They had a bit of a rough patch, But they got a new programmer and they are now keeping the community up to date with a monthly report. The game is amazing already, But you can see it still needs a lot of work.

[h1]Conclusion [b]8/10[/b][/h1]
It is a great game, even in its current state it is well worth the money, Especially if you like twin stick shooters, The game is a true unforgiving bullet hell rogue lite. It has bunch lot of unique mechanics, nice graphics and a great diversity in weapons and enemies. The game surely has the potentional to become a masterpiece.
